body: Ninja Gaiden II is Team Ninja's Xbox 360 action game, first released in North America on 3 June 2008. Ryu Hayabusa travels through a campaign of close combat against human and supernatural opponents, using a growing collection of weapons and ninja techniques. The sequel intensifies the speed and violence of the earlier game, asking the player to respond to several threats at once. An enemy who has been wounded can still be dangerous. Finishing an encounter therefore depends on reading what remains in front of Ryu rather than assuming an attack has settled it.

Obliteration Techniques allow Ryu to finish wounded enemies, but approaching them without care can expose him to a desperate counterattack. Blocking and evasive movement help create room for another response. Essence released during combat can restore resources or be drawn into an Ultimate Technique, giving the player a reason to decide when to collect it. Weapons such as claws, a scythe and paired swords change reach and rhythm. The challenge comes from connecting these actions under pressure, turning a brief opening into a controlled attack before another opponent interrupts.

Health partly recovers after a fight, while lasting damage limits how much returns without an item or a save statue. This structure encourages the player to finish a dangerous exchange, then consider what has been lost before continuing. The game was Tomonobu Itagaki's final directed release before leaving Tecmo. Ninja Gaiden Sigma 2 followed on PlayStation 3 in 2009 with substantial changes, and Ninja Gaiden 2 Black revisited the game in 2025. The original Xbox 360 version retains its own balance, enemy pressure and distinctive combat pace.
